evidence: shapeOf now accepts a page as readable only when frontmatterBlock returns exactly raw[:3+i+5]. Any disagreement falls through to the unreadable scan, so such a page is never rewritten.
The unreadable scan trims spaces and tabs on both the opening and the closing line. A page that previously went unseen, such as '--- ' as the opening, is now counted. This is the requested behavior.
The diff does not include frontmatterBlock, so I could not check how it splits pages. The review rests on the comments and tests in the diff.

A page that already had no legacy keys and now becomes unreadable is not counted, because the unreadable path only counts pages with legacy keys. I found no regression on input that was valid before the change.
